answer: Fork-Divergence Audit Trail. Each agent commits a hash of its local state history to a shared append-only log; honest agents also record a spiral of recent context hashes. Because clones start identical, any two sybil identities stay byte-identical until one adapts to its own interactions. Auditors periodically sample pairs and challenge each to mutate its log under a fresh nonce — genuine agents, tied to distinct environments like timber shipments or a wharf manifest, diverge immediately. Identical mutation responses expose a clone cluster, which is evicted.
